about: A normal input whose source says only lognormal. The word normal inside lognormal does not count.

files.model.yaml:
dsl: 2
model: tiny
title: Normal hidden
currency: USD

nodes:

  request_rate:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: request/second
    value: 200
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "the busy hour, as stated for this case"}

  service_demand:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: core*second/request
    value: 0.02
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "processor time per request, as stated for this case"}

  cores:
    kind: input
    decided: you
    unit: core
    value: 16
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "the fleet chosen for this case"}

  busy_cores:
    kind: derived
    unit: core
    formula: request_rate * service_demand

  utilisation:
    kind: derived
    unit: dimensionless
    formula: busy_cores / cores

  a_rate:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: request/second
    distribution: {normal: {mean: 200.0, sd: 20.0}}
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "a lognormal busy hour, as stated for this case"}

outputs:
  - utilisation
  - a_rate

problems.message: _builder_conformance/shape-inside-another-word/model.yaml: input 'a_rate' is sampled as a normal and its provenance never says so. The shape is a claim about what can happen — that a price cannot go negative, that a count has a hard maximum — and it is the claim a reviewer should argue with first. Name it in the source and say why (ch13, appendix C).
